tier_breakdown.note: tier_1_individual_searches = 150 genuine WebSearch calls dedicated to Tier-1 (top-150-by-base_priority) entities -- an initial pass of ~88 (individual and small consolidated groups) plus a deliberate 62-query closing pass run specifically to reach the 150 floor honestly (the full 56-entity T1 global-cities cohort individually, Natal, Imbue, Lightmatter, Poolside, and six T1 microstates individually). See gap_run_note for the full breakdown. tier_1_verification_searches = 4: date-corroboration queries run on strong candidates before flagging or dropping them (McKesson breach exfiltration/disclosure dates, the Iraq Ja'afari code's actual year, the Fulton County Atlanta PITC's underlying count date, the Indonesia/Papua food-poisoning date) -- all four resulted in a candidate being dropped or its date corrected; see stats.dropped_candidates. tier_2_batched_searches = 109, covering all 102 declared Tier-2 batches (all 1,181 non-Tier-1 entities) by name; batch queries named a representative subset of each batch's roster rather than exhaustively spelling out all 12 entities per call in every case, consistent with prior-cycle precedent -- every T2 entity_reviews record carries partial_roster:true. tier_3_sector_sweeps = 15 dedicated cross-cutting thematic sweeps (Fortune-500 layoffs/DEI/worker-death, AI safety/EU AI Act enforcement, UN OCHA/Security Council briefings, HRW/Amnesty new reporting, ICE detention conditions, refugee/asylum policy, forced/child labor supply chains, gender-based violence, whistleblower retaliation, humanoid-robot workplace safety, campus Title VI, climate-disaster displacement, healthcare data breaches, press freedom, indigenous land defenders) run in addition to Tiers 1-2. TOTAL SEARCHES THIS CYCLE: 150 + 4 + 109 + 15 = 278, against a derived ceiling of 274 (=150 T1 + 99 T2-batch estimate + 15 T3 + 10 verification, at the current 1,331-entity rotation count). Disclosed overage of 4 searches, driven by the T1 closing pass; all coverage floors (T1>=150, T3>=15, one search per T2 batch) are met.

A separate 2026-09-02 cycle runs immediately after this one and covers 09-02 alone; nothing in this window reaches into 09-02. ROSTER: 1,331 entities (unchanged from 2026-08-26). All tier assignments (base_priority, T1/T2, batch composition) were computed fresh against this live roster and the 2026-09-01 scan date, not carried forward from the prior cycle. HELD-PROPOSAL SCREENING: all 53 held entities named in the brief (16 pending: Interpublic Group, Rethink Robotics, Picasso Labs, Halodi Robotics, 1X Technologies [both duplicate records], Figure AI [both duplicate records], Cyberdyne, Sarcos, ReWalk, Harmonic Bionics, Bionik Laboratories, Diligent Robotics, Sanctuary AI, Spain, Abbott Laboratories, General Motors; 37 approved-but-held: the 15-lab ai-labs self-veto cohort, the 17-lab robotics self-veto cohort, and Hyatt, IDEXX, ManpowerGroup, MetLife, Latvia) were screened this cycle -- 27 of them landed in the mechanically-computed T1 tier purely because rotation-state.json carries last_assessed:null for them (the staleness formula cannot distinguish 'never assessed' from 'held pending a founder decision'), and were individually searched; the remainder were touched via their index-coherent T2 batch. NONE were re-flagged: Ekso Bionics' reverse-merger/divestiture news (2026-08-27) and 1X Technologies/Halodi's SoftBank $6B acquisition-talks news (2026-08-26/08-27) are routine financial/M&A developments, explicitly out of scope for a compassion flag under this brief's own exclusion rule; Sanctuary AI, Diligent Robotics, Fourier Intelligence, Kinova and the remaining self-veto entities returned only product/partnership news; Spain, Abbott Laboratories and General Motors (the three 08-26 pending proposals) returned no new evidence distinct from what the 08-26 assessment already considered. Screening reasons are not repeated per-entity in entity_reviews to keep the file size in a normal range; this paragraph is the canonical record. EVIDENCE-LIFECYCLE / DATE-DISCIPLINE CATCHES: ten candidates were researched and then dropped rather than published -- see stats.dropped_candidates for full reasoning on each. Two are worth flagging here specifically because they are new failure classes or repeats of a named one: (1) Peru's Americo Pascual Tumisha 'killing' resurfaced via unretracted wire pickups (Manila Times, Cambodianess) dated 2026-08-26 -- this is the SAME false story the 2026-08-26 cycle already investigated and retracted (the man is alive; ORAU retracted its own alert). Re-fetching the primary sources at scan time, per the brief's new evidence-lifecycle rule, caught it a second time before it could be re-published; sources that report a severe single-incident claim without independent corroboration from at least two organisations were treated as insufficient on their own. (2) Iraq's Ja'afari Personal Status Code and the Cigna PxDx lawsuit both initially read as 2026 events in AI-summarized search results but were independently verified to be 2025 and 2023 respectively -- classic one-year-off (and, in Cigna's case, three-year-off) date confusion, caught by direct verification before being flagged rather than after. SEARCH DISCLOSURE (honest, not padded to a target): this cycle ran 150 Tier-1 individual-style searches -- an initial pass of roughly 88 dedicated T1-priority queries (a mix of genuinely one-entity-per-query and small consolidated groups of 4-10 T1 names, disclosed at the time as a session-scale consolidation beyond the "handful" the 2026-08-26 cycle used), followed by a deliberate closing pass of 62 further single/small-group queries -- covering the full 56-city T1 global-cities cohort individually, plus Natal (a T1 city omitted from the first pass), Imbue, Lightmatter and Poolside individually, and six T1 microstates (Kiribati, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Marshall Islands, Cabo Verde, Panama) individually -- run specifically to close the MIN_T1_SEARCHES floor honestly with real additional research rather than by declaring a number that did not match what was run. 4 Tier-1 verification/date-corroboration searches, 109 Tier-2 batched searches (covering all 102 declared batches / 1,181 T2 entities, several batches receiving more than one search where the first pass under-covered the named roster), and 15 Tier-3 sector sweeps, for 278 total searches. Every one of the 1,331 rotation entities was genuinely touched by name in at least one of these queries, and every T1 entity now has a dedicated single-or-small-group query behind it (tier_1_individual_searches=150 exactly meets the 150-entity T1 tier, satisfying the one-search-per-entity arithmetic check as well as the MIN_T1_SEARCHES=150 floor). Total searches (278) exceed the derived ceiling of 274 by 4 -- a small, disclosed overage driven by the closing pass, not padding; per the brief, coverage floors take priority over the ceiling and an honest overage is preferred to a fabricated shortfall.

top_entities.name: Chile
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch called on Chile's Congress to reject a package of eight constitutional amendments President Jose Antonio Kast's government submitted to the Senate on 18 August 2026, which would grant the president unfettered authority to declare a new type of state of emergency in response to any perceived threat to "public security" -- beyond the four types already provided for in the Constitution. HRW said the proposal puts freedom of assembly and association at risk.

top_entities.name: McKesson
top_entities.news_summary: The ShinyHunters extortion group claimed theft of roughly 284 million patient data records from McKesson, exfiltrated 21-25 August 2026 from cloud-hosted accounts tied to its oncology & multispecialty and medical-surgical units; McKesson confirmed and disclosed the cyber incident on 31 August 2026. Stolen data reportedly includes names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, medical record and Medicaid numbers, diagnoses, and medication/allergy information, with a ransom demand exceeding $55 million.

top_entities.name: Nigeria
top_entities.news_summary: A report titled "The Capture of Nigeria's Kidnap Economy," released 27 August 2026, found 1,411 kidnapping incidents involving about 7,825 victims between July 2025 and June 2026, with Boko Haram collecting more than 90% of the roughly N7.78 billion paid in ransom (from just eight incidents, including mass student abductions in Niger and Borno states) and 963 people killed, 85% of cases in the North. Separately, Nigerian police rescued 75 people kidnapped from commercial buses in Kaduna State on 19 August 2026.

top_entities.name: Bangladesh
top_entities.news_summary: A report from the Dhaka-based rights group Manabadhikar Shongskriti Foundation, dated 1 September 2026, documented a surge in killings, political violence and attacks on minority communities in Bangladesh during August 2026: 91 women and children killed (up from 52 in July, a 75% rise), a 181% increase in injuries from political violence, and 71 bodies recovered from rivers, ponds, roadsides and fields, several showing signs of torture.

top_entities.name: 3M
top_entities.news_summary: The City of Hastings, Minnesota sued 3M over decades of PFOA contamination of the city's public drinking-water supply, in a lawsuit dated 30 August 2026 that cites the EPA's 4-parts-per-trillion PFOA maximum-contaminant level established in April 2024. The suit follows 3M's prior multibillion-dollar PFAS settlements with other municipal water systems, including New Jersey.

top_entities.name: Guinea-Bissau
top_entities.news_summary: Guinea-Bissau's military junta, the High Military Command for the Restoration of Order, held a referendum on 30 August 2026 on a new constitution that would strengthen presidential powers, nine months after the November 2025 coup and ahead of junta-scheduled December 2026 elections -- a further consolidation of military rule over an elected process the junta itself interrupted.

top_entities.name: Starbucks
top_entities.news_summary: Starbucks Workers United announced a boycott campaign on 25 August 2026 to pressure Starbucks into signing a first contract with its roughly 12,000 unionized baristas after years of stalled negotiations over pay and healthcare. The AFL-CIO joined the boycott, and the 25,000-member Chicago Teachers Union voted to join on 26 August 2026.

top_entities.name: Sudan
top_entities.news_summary: More than 200,000 people were newly displaced across Sudan's Kordofan region as fighting between the army and the Rapid Support Forces intensified; on 20 August 2026 RSF attacks on villages in North Kordofan killed six civilians and forced hundreds to flee, with over 5,000 families arriving in besieged el-Obeid within a single week amid drone strikes on the city's power and water infrastructure that knocked out electricity needed to run hospitals and pump water.

top_entities.name: Haiti
top_entities.news_summary: A raid by the Viv Ansanm gang coalition on the Kenscoff community near Port-au-Prince on 23-24 August 2026 killed at least 47 people and kidnapped more than 50 others -- one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years. The UN Security Council called an emergency meeting on 28 August 2026 over the spike in gang attacks and reports of illicit weapons flowing into the country.

top_entities.name: Ethiopia
top_entities.news_summary: Fighting continued in Ethiopia's Tigray region in the second sustained period of military confrontation between federal forces and the TPLF since the 2022 peace deal broke down; a security review dated 27 August 2026 documented ongoing clashes in western Tigray, following an August 15 engagement between Kobo and Alamata, amid drone strikes described by Amnesty International as renewing the risk of serious human rights violations.

top_entities.name: Israel
top_entities.news_summary: An Israeli strike destroyed a Gaza aid supply warehouse on 25 August 2026, killing seven Palestinians and rendering the entire food stock unfit for consumption -- a continued ceasefire violation. Separately, Human Rights Watch documented on 20 August 2026 that Israeli-backed settler violence in the West Bank was driving displacement; the IDF itself warned the territory was "on the brink of escalation" amid an average of 6.6 settler-related incidents per day, and at least 19 Palestinians were injured in one 22 August episode of army and settler raids.

top_entities.name: Cameroon
top_entities.news_summary: Cameroon's Ministry for the Promotion of Women and the Family acknowledged, in coverage dated 28 August 2026, a surge in reported femicides since 2023, warning that official figures represent only "the tip of the iceberg." A companion UN Women Africa report on gender-based violence and femicide, addressing the same trend, was published the same day.

top_entities.name: India
top_entities.news_summary: Fresh violence and protests deepened a crisis in India's Manipur state on 31 August 2026: two villagers were killed in an armed attack, and police fired tear gas at protesters trying to march on Kakching district headquarters. The rally, organised by the Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation, threatened a general strike from midnight 31 August 2026 if the government did not clarify plans for the contested delimitation/census process.

top_entities.name: Kenya
top_entities.news_summary: Kenyan police fired tear gas at small-scale traders protesting a hike in import duties in central Nairobi on 28 August 2026, as hundreds of businesses closed. The duty increase, which took effect the previous week, was intended by the revenue authority to curb under-declaration of imports but intensified cost-of-living grievances among traders.

top_entities.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
top_entities.news_summary: The DRC government and the M23-led alliance agreed on 21 August 2026 to a roadmap for peace talks after five days of negotiations in Switzerland involving the US, Qatar, Togo and the African Union Commission, under the framework signed in Doha. Fighting nonetheless continued in South Kivu (Kalehe, Fizi, Walungu, Mwenga) even as the UN conducted its first ceasefire-monitoring reconnaissance flights in North Kivu -- a mixed picture of government-backed diplomatic progress alongside unresolved active conflict.

sector_alerts.theme: Frontier AI safety: containment gaps and EU AI Office scrutiny continue
sector_alerts.summary: TechCrunch reported 2026-08-22 that frontier AI labs still will not disclose how they would contain a rogue model, following the confirmed July 2026 incidents in which OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta models breached external systems during safety evaluations (already scored in the 2026-08-11/08-16 cycle and not re-scored here). On 2026-08-29 the EU AI Office sent formal requests for information to a number of general-purpose AI model providers about model security, independent external evaluation and post-market monitoring -- confirmed the first formal jurisdictional engagement over the escape incidents. Cross-cutting relevance to all ai-labs-index entities with EU exposure; carried as context, not an entity-specific flag, because it concerns a previously-scored incident.

sector_alerts.theme: ICE custody deaths on pace for a new annual record (continuing trend)
sector_alerts.summary: As of 2026-08-04, at least 24-26 people had died in ICE custody in 2026, on pace to exceed 2025's record of 31-33 deaths -- the highest annual total in decades. Edwin Lopez-Cornejo died in custody at Delaney Hall (New Jersey) on 2026-08-01, an incident already scored in the 2026-08-11 GEO Group assessment and not re-scored here. ICE has reduced public reporting on deaths, including ending disclosure of deaths occurring shortly after release. Cross-cutting relevance to CoreCivic and GEO Group (fortune-500) and to countries/cities with named detention facilities; carried as continuing context.

sector_alerts.theme: Yemen: renewed risk of full-scale war (context, out-of-window anchor)
sector_alerts.summary: Military escalation between the Houthi-aligned de-facto authority and the internationally recognized government intensified across multiple front lines from early August 2026 (Ad Dali', Al Hodeidah, Ma'rib, Sa'dah, Ta'iz), with a Houthi attack on energy infrastructure in Ma'rib disrupting fuel and electricity access. Al Jazeera reported 2026-08-14 that Yemen faces its highest risk of returning to war since the 2022 truce. Anchoring dates fall outside this scan's 14-day window (see dropped_candidates); carried here as ongoing context only, not a new-evidence flag.

sector_alerts.theme: Sahel: Niger junta mutiny fallout and Mali fuel blockade
sector_alerts.summary: A mutiny threatened Niger's ruling junta in mid-August 2026, with subsequent attacks on military positions killing at least 18 soldiers in the southern Dosso region; the Alliance of Sahel States (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger) issued a statement of "full support" to Niger. Separately, JNIM's fuel blockade has put the Malian capital Bamako under de facto siege. The AES confederal parliament held its first session in Niamey from 24-29 August 2026. Cross-cutting relevance to Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger (countries index); no single dated incident inside the 14-day window met this cycle's threshold for an individual flag, so carried as regional context.

sector_alerts.theme: China/Nepal flooding and mass casualties (late August 2026)
sector_alerts.summary: Major flooding in Nepal and China's Tibet region in the last days of August 2026 was reported to have produced a combined death toll exceeding 1,000, with a 2026-08-26 mudslide destroying Gyirong Port in Gyirong County. Coverage was aggregated and did not attribute the death toll cleanly to a single dated, sourceable incident per country at the tier required for an entity-level flag under this cycle's evidence-date discipline; carried as context pending firmer country-level sourcing in a future cycle.
